name: Pursue a P3 project as construction partner
summary: In a public-private partnership the public sponsor picks a consortium of equity investors, a design-builder and a maintenance provider to design, build, finance and maintain a hospital, school or courthouse for decades. The contractor's P3 director forms the consortium, answers the RFQ and, if shortlisted, leads design development, estimating, scheduling and risk review for a fixed design-build price that must fit the sponsor's affordability cap. Contracts counsel, treasury and the executive team sign off on the risk, security and equity commitments, and the winning team negotiates to commercial and financial close with lenders. It is slow and costly because one pursuit runs for about a year, ties up a design manager and a team of estimators, costs hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars, and is lost two times in three with only an honorarium in return.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about $1.5B annual revenue that acts as design-builder and minority equity investor in P3 consortia through its capital arm.
baseline.notes: Describes traditional design-build-finance(-maintain) pursuits with fixed RFP-stage prices as run in 2019-2022; Infrastructure Ontario's progressive P3 model announced in 2021 is outside this baseline.

unit_of_work: one P3 pursuit, from screening the opportunity to financial close or loss
trigger: A public sponsor (Infrastructure Ontario, Alberta Infrastructure or similar) announces a P3 project in a market update or posts an RFQ, and the opportunity pipeline flags it.
end_state: Financial close is reached and the design-build subcontract is handed to contract award, or the pursuit is closed (declined, not shortlisted, lost with honorarium claimed, or cancelled).

volume.seasonality: Driven by provincial infrastructure plans and sponsor market updates rather than the calendar.

evidence.note: One to four new pursuits a year; with pursuits lasting 12 to 15 months this gives one to three pursuits running at once, which matches the organisation file's 1 to 3 pursuit-months a month.

resources.name: Pickup trucks for superintendents, foremen and safety staff

steps.name: Screen the P3 opportunity and draft a pursuit budget
steps.description: The P3 director reads the sponsor's market notice and procurement documents, assesses the project size, risk allocation, competition and likely partners, and drafts a pursuit budget covering internal staff, design consultants and advisors and the honorarium recoverable if the bid loses.

evidence.note: Bid costs and honorarium as described; screening effort is an estimate.

steps.name: Approve the pursuit and its budget
steps.description: The VP of business development takes the pursuit case to the executive team, which approves the spend, the bonding and letter of credit capacity it will tie up and the proposed equity role of the company's investment arm, or declines.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: executive approval of P3 pursuit budgets and equity commitments

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Form the consortium and agree teaming terms
steps.description: The P3 director negotiates, over several weeks of partner meetings, with the lead equity partner, facility maintenance provider and architect on roles, exclusivity, shared bid costs, the split of any honorarium and key commercial positions, and fixes the team for the RFQ.

evidence.note: Consortium make-up (equity lead, design-builder, architect, maintenance provider, financing partners) from the Concert-Bird Partners example; negotiation effort is an estimate.

steps.name: Review teaming and exclusivity agreements
steps.description: Contracts counsel drafts or marks up the teaming agreement, confidentiality and exclusivity terms and the outline design-build subcontract positions, and flags uncapped liabilities before the company signs.

control.basis: Corporate contract review policy: legal sign-off on joint venture and teaming agreements

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Prepare the RFQ response
steps.description: Once the sponsor posts the RFQ, the proposal coordinator assembles the consortium's experience, key individuals' resumes, safety record, financial capacity and surety support letters into the sponsor's RFQ format and coordinates partner inputs to the submission deadline.

error.defect_description: Partner information or key individual commitments are incomplete.

evidence.note: RFQ step with a closing date about four weeks after posting (Alberta 2020); hours are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for RFQ evaluation and RFP issue
steps.description: The sponsor evaluates the RFQ responses, shortlists usually three teams and later issues the RFP and data room to them; teams not shortlisted stop here.

evidence.note: Alberta RFQ closed 8 October 2020 and the three-team shortlist was announced 6 November 2020 (29 days); the shortlist share for one firm is an estimate.

steps.name: Kick off the RFP stage and engage designers
steps.description: The P3 director sets up the bid schedule, responsibility matrix and data room access, signs the design consultants on pursuit terms, and starts the weekly design, cost and commercial meetings with the equity lead.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Manage design development to the output specifications
steps.description: The design manager runs the architects and engineers through RFP-stage design, waits on each consultant drawing issue, checks every drawing set against the sponsor's output specifications and affordability cap, and logs compliance and open design risks.

error.defect_description: A specification requirement is missed and found by the sponsor's compliance review.

evidence.note: Traditional P3 RFPs require fixed prices based on proponents' own designs; hours are estimates (about 0.7 FTE for 8 months).

steps.name: Visit the site and existing facilities
steps.description: The preconstruction manager travels to the site for the sponsor's scheduled visit, walks the existing buildings, access routes and utility points with the design team, and records constraints for logistics and phasing.

control.basis: Site-specific orientation and personal protective equipment required by the owner for visitors to an operating facility or construction site

evidence.note: Scheduled site visits are a standard part of Canadian P3 RFPs; travel time and vehicle use are estimates.

steps.name: Estimate each design iteration
steps.description: Estimators take off quantities from each design iteration, price self-performed work and budget trade costs, compare the total with the affordability cap and report the gap to the design and commercial teams every few weeks.

error.defect_description: Quantities or scope gaps in the cost plan.

evidence.note: Bid cost of 0.5% of value implies a large estimating effort; hours (about 1,400 h across a team of estimators) are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Obtain trade pricing and design-assist input
steps.description: Estimators issue mechanical, electrical, envelope and structural packages through trade tendering for budget prices and design-assist advice, then level the replies by scope.

error.defect_description: Trade exclusions not carried in the levelled price.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Develop construction schedule and phasing
steps.description: The scheduler builds the design, permit, construction and commissioning schedule to the sponsor's availability date, tests it with the superintendent assigned to the bid, and prepares the schedule narrative.

evidence.note: A fixed target availability date (31 May 2024 for the Alberta schools) is the schedule constraint; hours are estimates.

steps.name: Attend commercially confidential meetings
steps.description: The P3 director prepares questions and comments on the draft project agreement and output specifications and attends the series of commercially confidential meetings the sponsor holds with each team.

evidence.note: Commercially confidential meetings with proponents are part of IO procurements; preparation time is an estimate.

steps.name: Review project agreement and design-build subcontract
steps.description: Contracts counsel reviews the project agreement flow-down into the design-build subcontract, including liquidated damages, liability caps, relief events and security, and negotiates positions with the equity lead and its lenders' counsel.

control.basis: Corporate contract review policy: legal sign-off on P3 risk allocation before price submission

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Arrange proposal security and surety support
steps.description: The treasury manager arranges the letter of credit or bid bond the RFP requires and obtains surety letters confirming performance and payment security for the design-build subcontract.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Review price and risk contingency
steps.description: The chief estimator leads a price review and risk workshop on the cost plan, trade prices, escalation, design development allowance and contingency, and decides whether the price meets the affordability cap or needs another round of value engineering.

control.basis: Estimating department review policy: senior estimator sign-off on every priced submission

next.condition: over the cap or risk too high

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Run a value engineering round
steps.description: The design manager works with the architects, trades and equity lead on design changes that cut cost without breaking the output specifications, and estimators reprice the changed elements.

evidence.note: Affordability constraints and pressure for value engineering on fixed RFP-stage prices are named by IO; frequency is an estimate.

steps.name: Prepare bid summary for executive approval
steps.description: The P3 director writes the bid summary with the design-build price, margin, contingency, key project agreement risks, security and equity commitments for the executive bid approval meeting.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Obtain executive bid approval
steps.description: The VP of business development presents the bid summary to the CEO, COO and CFO, who approve the price and risk position, set conditions or ask for changes; board notice is given for the largest bids.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: all P3 bids require executive bid approval

next.condition: approved subject to further cost reduction

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Assemble the technical submission
steps.description: The proposal coordinator compiles design drawings, narratives, schedule, construction methodology, quality and safety plans into the sponsor's submission format with the partners' sections.

error.defect_description: Cross-references or forms inconsistent between partners' sections.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Hand the design-build price to the equity lead and submit
steps.description: The P3 director issues the signed design-build price, schedule and cash flow to the equity lead for the financial model, confirms the committed price matches the approval, and the consortium submits its technical and financial submissions.

error.defect_description: Cash flow or price in the financial model does not match the approved design-build price.

evidence.note: Fixed price at RFP stage (IO); financing provided by the equity partners, including the contractor's own capital arm (Alberta example).

steps.name: Wait for sponsor evaluation
steps.description: The sponsor evaluates technical compliance and the financial offers, and names a preferred proponent; the losing teams are told and offered debriefs.

evidence.note: Three shortlisted teams; the RFP process completed in July 2021 with contract by end of September; a one-in-three win share is an estimate.

steps.name: Negotiate to commercial close
steps.description: The P3 director works with the equity lead, sponsor and lenders to finalise the project agreement, design-build subcontract, schedule and security package, and answers the lenders' technical advisor's due diligence questions on design, schedule and cost.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Wait for lenders' due diligence and financial close
steps.description: Lenders, their technical advisor and the sponsor complete due diligence, credit approvals and closing documents, and financial close takes place on the agreed date.

evidence.note: RFP process completed July 2021 and financial close announced 29 September 2021 for the Alberta schools; failure share is an estimate.

steps.name: Sign the design-build subcontract
steps.description: The VP of business development signs the design-build subcontract and the company's equity documents after confirming they match the approved bid and the bonding is in place.

control.basis: Signing authority: contracts above a threshold signed by an officer

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Hand over to contract award and project startup
steps.description: The P3 director hands the bid documents, design-build subcontract, schedule and cost plan to the contract award team and the project leadership, and records the win in the CRM.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of Canadian general contractors.

steps.name: Claim the honorarium and attend the debrief
steps.description: The P3 director attends the sponsor's debrief, records scores and lessons, and with the equity lead invoices the honorarium and splits it among partners under the teaming agreement.

evidence.note: Honorarium to unsuccessful proponents (IO), about $1 million (DCN, 2006); timing is an estimate.

exceptions.name: Price over the affordability cap
exceptions.description: The reviewed price exceeds the sponsor's affordability cap or carries too much risk, so the team runs one or more value engineering rounds before executive approval.

exceptions.name: Executive asks for further cost reduction
exceptions.description: The executive approves on condition of a lower price or contingency, sending the team back into value engineering days before submission.

exceptions.name: Not shortlisted
exceptions.description: The consortium is not among the three teams invited to the RFP, so the pursuit stops after the RFQ with only screening, teaming and RFQ costs spent.

exceptions.name: Close fails or project cancelled
exceptions.description: The sponsor cancels or lenders do not close, leaving the preferred proponent with sunk costs.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from screening to the end of the pursuit, all outcomes

evidence.note: Derived: more than half of pursuits end at the go decision or the RFQ shortlist (about 2 to 4 months in), while shortlisted pursuits run to evaluation or financial close at 11 to 15 months (Alberta 2020-21 timeline). The outcome shares are the author's estimates.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from screening the opportunity to financial close (winning pursuits only)

evidence.note: Alberta five-schools bundle: RFQ posted about 11 September 2020, financial close 29 September 2021 (383 days), plus one to two months of screening and teaming before the RFQ. Ontario hospital P3s often ran longer.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from RFQ closing to shortlist announcement

evidence.note: RFQ closed 8 October 2020; shortlist reported 6 November 2020.

benchmarks.unit: percent of project value (out-of-pocket, about $500,000 on $100 million)
benchmarks.population: Contractor estimate for Canadian P3 bids, reported 2006

evidence.note: Older than the reference period; used as the only published Canadian figure the author could open.

pain_points.description: A pursuit ties up a design manager and several estimators for most of a year, and two pursuits out of three are lost with only an honorarium in return.

evidence.note: Bid cost and honorarium figures; three shortlisted teams per bundle.

pain_points.description: Fixed prices on early designs push teams through repeated value engineering rounds to meet the affordability cap, and risk the design-builder carries after close.

evidence.note: IO states market concern about fixed price bids at the RFP stage based on early designs and about affordability constraints.

pain_points.description: Risk positions must be agreed across the sponsor, equity lead and lenders, so legal review and commercial meetings stretch the schedule.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from the number of parties in a P3 consortium.

sources.title: P3 RFQ released to build Alberta schools
sources.supports: Article of 11 September 2020: Alberta posted an RFQ for a design-build-finance-maintain bundle of five high schools; the RFQ closed 8 October 2020; up to three proponents to be shortlisted and invited to the RFP stage; contract expected by the end of September 2021.

sources.title: Alberta issues RFP for schools to be constructed through P3
sources.supports: Article of 6 November 2020: three shortlisted consortia, including Concert-Bird Partners (Concert Infrastructure lead, BR2 Architecture design, Bird Construction construction, Ainsworth maintenance, Concert and Bird Capital financing); RFP process to be completed in July 2021 and contract in place by end of September 2021; schools to open September 2024.

sources.title: Financial close achieved for five Alberta schools under DBFM contract
sources.publisher: Bird Construction Inc. via Cision Newswire
sources.supports: Release of 29 September 2021: Concert-Bird Partners (Bird Capital LP, Bird Design-Build Construction Inc., Concert Infrastructure, Ainsworth, BR2 Architecture, Wright Construction Western) reached financial close on a contract of over $300 million; 30-year maintenance term; financing arranged by Bird Capital and Concert; target total availability 31 May 2024.

sources.title: Progressive Procurement P3: Q&As
sources.publisher: Infrastructure Ontario (hosted by the Ontario General Contractors Association newsletter)
sources.supports: In a traditional P3 proponents must submit fixed price bids at the RFP stage based on early designs; the progressive model was introduced because of affordability, competition and risk-transfer concerns; traditional RFPs require detailed design and demonstrated financing commitments; commercially confidential meetings are held with proponents; an honorarium (proposal fee) is offered to unsuccessful proponents.

sources.title: The debate over PPP honoraria
sources.supports: Honoraria of about $1 million help offset the cost of losing a P3 bid; a contractor estimated out-of-pocket bid costs at about 0.5% of project value ($500,000 on a $100 million job) and about $1 million on a $300 million job.

assumptions: The organisation file defines the unit of work as one P3 pursuit-month; this file documents one whole pursuit instead, because the steps (RFQ, RFP, close) happen once per pursuit. One to four new pursuits a year with a 12 to 15 month duration is equivalent to the organisation file's 1 to 3 pursuit-months a month.
The RFQ response is written inside this process; the organisation file's owner prequalification process (bd-prequalification) only sends prequal submissions to public owners.

Loaded costs and titles come from the organisation file (wage x 1.35 for salaried staff). Design consultant fees, advisor fees and the equity arm's work are outside the labour cost because they are not company roles in this process.
Roles needed but not listed for this process in the organisation file: proposal-coordinator, chief-estimator, scheduler, precon-manager and treasury-manager.

Shortlist share (0.55) and win share after shortlisting (0.35) are estimates for a national contractor that teams with established equity partners; with three shortlisted teams a one-in-three win rate is the neutral expectation.

Simulated winning pursuits reach financial close in a median of about 380 days against the 420-day benchmark; the gap is within the spread of Canadian P3 timelines (the Alberta RFQ-to-close period alone was 383 days) and was left rather than padding waits.
Simulated steps run in sequence; design management, site visit and estimating overlap in practice (concurrent_with), and their touch time stands in for the RFP-stage elapsed time.
